paramInfo.play.touch: How hard you have to play. Light: quiet playing already reaches the loud, bright layers. Heavy: you need to dig in.
paramInfo.play.dynamics: The range between soft and loud notes. 100% is the recorded piano's own range.
paramInfo.tone.bright: Tilts every note's partials: more or less treble per octave of overtones, like harder or softer hammers.
paramInfo.tone.hammer: The knock of the hammer and key at the start of each note.
paramInfo.string.unison: How far the two or three strings of each note are out of tune with each other. This is the slow beating in a sustained note. 100% is as measured.
paramInfo.string.stretch: The recorded piano's stretch tuning: low notes flatter and high notes sharper, as a tuner sets a real piano to match its stiff strings. 0% is plain equal temperament.
paramInfo.string.sustain: How long notes ring. 100% is as measured.
paramInfo.string.damper: How long the dampers take to stop a note when you let go of the key. Keys above E6 have no dampers, as on a grand.
paramInfo.space.width: Stereo width of the two microphones the piano was measured with.
paramInfo.space.room: A small room around the piano. The measurements are close-miked, so 0 is the dry piano.
paramInfo.tone.attack: How long each note takes to swell in at the strike. 100% is as measured for each key, from the recordings.
paramInfo.tone.body: The soundboard and room ringing on after each strike: the echo-like tail most audible on high notes. 0 dB is as measured. The key's damper stops it when you let go (above E6, where there are no dampers, it rings on).
